questions.stem: Which of the following is the best definition of a private limited company?
options: A company with its own legal identity whose shareholders have limited liability and whose shares are not sold publicly
A company whose shares are traded on a stock exchange
A business owned and run by one person
A business owned by two or more people with unlimited liability
questions.why: The defining features are separate legal identity, limited liability, and shares that cannot be offered to the general public.
whyNot: That is a public limited company.
That is a sole trader.
That is a partnership.

questions.stem: Which term is defined as: an arrangement in which a franchisee pays to trade under an established brand using the franchisor's business model?
options: Franchising
Social enterprise
Flotation
Incorporation
questions.why: The franchisee buys a proven system, brand and support and accepts fees, royalties and strict rules in return. The franchisor expands using someone else's capital.
whyNot: A social enterprise trades to achieve a social objective.
Flotation is offering shares to the public.
Incorporation creates a company with separate legal identity.

questions.stem: What is the main advantage of operating as a sole trader?
options: It is fast and cheap to start, with complete control and all the profit
Personal assets are protected from business debts
It is the easiest form for raising large sums
Accounts do not have to be prepared at all
questions.why: Minimal formality, immediate decisions, total control and every pound of profit. The trade-off is unlimited liability and difficulty raising finance.
whyNot: A sole trader has unlimited liability, so personal assets are exposed.
It is the hardest of the three main forms for raising finance.
Accounts are still needed, for tax if nothing else.

questions.stem: What is the sharpest risk in a partnership that students often overlook?
options: Each partner is liable for the business decisions of the others
Partnerships cannot raise any finance
Partnerships must have exactly two owners
Partners cannot share profits
questions.why: With unlimited liability and joint responsibility, one partner's poor decision can expose the others' personal assets. It is the main reason a written partnership agreement matters.
whyNot: Partnerships raise finance from partners' capital, loans and trade credit.
Two or more; there is no fixed maximum in most jurisdictions.
Sharing profits is a defining feature.

questions.stem: Why does a partnership need a written partnership agreement?
options: Without one, statutory default rules apply to profit shares and disputes
It is required before the business can open a bank account
It converts the partnership into a company
It gives the partners limited liability
questions.why: The agreement sets out shares, responsibilities, decision-making and what happens if a partner leaves. In its absence, default legal provisions decide, and they may not be what the partners wanted.
whyNot: A bank account can be opened without one, though banks often ask to see it.
Incorporation is a separate legal process.
Liability depends on the legal form, not on the agreement.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a disadvantage of becoming a private limited company?
options: Accounts must be filed publicly, so competitors can see them
The owners become personally liable for all debts
The business cannot continue if an owner leaves
It cannot employ any staff
questions.why: Incorporation brings registration costs, filing requirements, director duties and a loss of privacy. Filed accounts are visible to rivals, suppliers and customers.
whyNot: Incorporation gives limited liability, reducing personal exposure.
A company continues regardless of changes in ownership. That is one of its advantages.
Companies employ staff normally.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best definition of a lifestyle business?
options: A business run to support the owner's chosen way of life rather than to maximise growth
A business selling health and fitness products
A business run entirely online
A business that trades to achieve a social objective
questions.why: Deliberately limited in scale, and entirely rational: it is profit satisficing applied to the whole business. Treating it as a failure of ambition misreads the objective.
whyNot: The sector is irrelevant; the term describes the owner's objective.
That is an online business.
That is a social enterprise.

questions.stem: What is the central trade-off in a stock market flotation?
options: It raises large sums of capital and disperses ownership, so control is lost
It raises capital and requires no disclosure
It gives limited liability for the first time
It removes the need to make a profit
questions.why: Flotation solves a finance problem and creates a control problem. Ownership is dispersed, strategy becomes public, short-term shareholder pressure arrives, and a founder can be voted out of their own company.
whyNot: A plc faces far more disclosure, not less.
A private limited company already has limited liability.
Public shareholders increase the pressure to deliver profit.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a disadvantage of buying a franchise?
options: Ongoing royalties and strict rules limit the franchisee's freedom
There is no established brand to trade under
The franchisee must develop the business model themselves
There is no training or support available
questions.why: You buy a proven system and pay for it continuously, and you follow someone else's rules. You also carry the risk of reputational damage caused by other franchisees.
whyNot: An established brand is the main thing being bought.
The model comes from the franchisor; that is the point.
Training and support are normally part of the package.

questions.stem: At what point does incorporating typically become worthwhile for a small guesthouse owner?
options: When they borrow significant sums or operate more than one property
As soon as they open, regardless of scale
Only once they employ more than fifty staff
Never, because guesthouses cannot incorporate
questions.why: Limited liability is worth its cost when there is a large exposure and personal assets to protect. Substantial borrowing or multiple properties is the point where a failure would otherwise reach the family home.
whyNot: For a single tiny property with no debt, the cost and filing outweigh the protection.
Headcount is not the trigger; the amount at risk is.
Any business can incorporate.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of an online business as a form?
options: Low start-up costs and national or global reach from day one
Very high barriers to entry, keeping competition out
No need to be found by customers
Guaranteed profitability
questions.why: No premises and a wide reach make it cheap to start. The same low barriers mean intense competition, and success depends entirely on being discoverable.
whyNot: Barriers are very low, which is a drawback as well as an advantage.
Being found is the central challenge of an online business.
Nothing guarantees profitability.
